                    ### Question
                    A 78-year-old man suffers a fall in a nursing home and is brought to the emergency room. A right hip fracture is diagnosed, and he is treated with a closed reduction with internal fixation under spinal anesthesia. On the second postoperative day, the patient complains of pain in the lower abdomen and states that he has not urinated since the surgery. An ultrasound shows increased bladder size and volume. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of the drug which is most commonly used to treat this patient’s condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Parasympathetic agonist
opb. Sympathetic agonist
opc. Parasympathetic antagonist
opd. Alpha-blocker
ope. Beta-blocker

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Postoperative urinary retention, common in elderly patients post-surgery involving spinal anesthesia, is due to impaired autonomic nervous system function affecting bladder control. Alpha-blockers are used to treat this by relaxing smooth muscle in the bladder neck and prostate, facilitating urine flow. This mechanism aligns with their role as alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonists, supported by evidence linking spinal anesthesia's impact on bladder function and the pharmacological management of its complications.
